labctl.notes: exec: labctl exec gt40 "<cmd>" (ssh root@:5828, key bridge_key) reaches the Debian KIOSK, not the PDP-11 — the simulated machine has no shell. Light-pen exhibit: labctl type/key do nothing here; drive it with tiles/gt40/pen-drive.py (QMP abs move + button 1).

tileEnv.SH_FIXTURE_DESC: DEC GT40 (1973) at the first seconds of a fresh lunar descent: the LEM in the upper left with its descent engine firing, four telemetry readouts across the top (HEIGHT ~17000-19000 feet, DISTANCE ~-15000 to -21000, VER VEL ~-490, HOR VEL ~880 — the exact digits differ by a second or two of flight from bake to bake), the 75% throttle bar and the two pairs of rotation arrows down the right edge, the twelve-item telemetry menu (HEIGHT, ALTITUDE, DISTANCE, FUEL LEFT, WEIGHT, THRUST, ANGLE, VER VEL, HOR VEL, VER ACC, HOR ACC, SECONDS) under them, and the mountainous lunar horizon across the bottom — green vectors on black, drawn by Open SIMH's VT11 at crt=vr17 scale=1 hspace=narrow in a 1024x1024 SDL window centred on a 1280x1024 X root. The exhibit is self-sustaining: the LEM falls for about two minutes, crashes, and the program restarts itself, a 135 s loop. LIGHT-PEN exhibit: the menu, the rotation arrows and the throttle bar are all selected by pointing; there is no keyboard input of any kind.

museum.blurb: A PDP-11 with a vector processor bolted to it and a light pen on a cord: no pixels, no keyboard worth using, just an electron beam drawing lines exactly where the program tells it. The 1973 Lunar Lander it is running was written to show the machine off, and it still does.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs Open SIMH's pdp11 simulator with the VT11 vector display, executing the original lunar.lda paper tape that ships inside the MIT-licensed Open SIMH tree — no external media, no staged asset, nothing to license. The exhibit is self-sustaining: the LEM falls for about two minutes, crashes, and the program restarts itself, so the golden rests at the first seconds of a fresh descent. THE ONLY POINTER-ONLY EXHIBIT IN THE COLLECTION and the only one where a light pen is the historically correct input device: the telemetry menu, the rotation arrows and the throttle bar are all driven by pointing, and there is no keyboard input of any kind (Open SIMH wires the pen to mouse button 1, so the pen is on the glass only while the button is held). No archetype models a vector CRT with a light pen; mono-terminal is a deliberate fallback, chosen because it is the only monochrome DEC-style CRT in the set. Displayed on the larger VR17 tube (crt=vr17) rather than the GT40's own VR14, because SIMH's VR14 model clips the twelve-item menu mid-word. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/gt40.md.

reset.fixture: The first seconds of a fresh lunar descent — the LEM in the upper left with its engine firing, ~18000 feet, a full tank, the 75% throttle bar and the twelve-item telemetry menu down the right edge — in Open SIMH's VT11 at crt=vr17 scale=1 hspace=narrow, a 1024x1024 window centred on a 1280x1024 X root. The program restarts itself after each crash, so the bake rides that loop: scripts/build-guests/tiles/gt40.sh waits for the "NO SURVIVORS" message and then for the restart it triggers, which is why reset always hands a visitor a NEW GAME rather than the middle of somebody else's doomed trajectory. Light-pen route certified 2026-08-09 after the bake, by framebuffer: with the pointer parked the menu column is dead still (blink range 0 over 20 samples), a pen touch on ANGLE makes that item blink (range 376 — the program's own acknowledgement that the pen hit a vector), and loadvm golden clears the selection again (range 0). Pointer-only exhibit; no keyboard input of any kind; AC97 card present for device-set parity, but the GT40 is silent.

notes: Open SIMH is built INTO the tile overlay (the amiga.sh precedent); the frozen bridge base does not carry it. bridge-base.sh needs the matching addition for a from-scratch NVMe rebuild — see docs/guests/gt40.md.
